observations: Photo 0: a wooden shelf in a parts shop crammed with dozens of used car engine and gearbox mounts of many shapes and sizes.
Photo 0: round rubber-and-steel mounts, bracket mounts and cylindrical bush mounts, mixed together; several tied with plastic string as sets.
Photo 0: many mounts are heavily rusted (top left bracket mount, left side brackets); rubber looks dry and dirty on several.
Photo 0: one black cylindrical mount top right has handwriting in white marker, something like 'Ekondo... innocent', a shop note, not a part number.
Photo 0: a watermark reads something like 'POSTED ON ... KINGSLEY IDEH'; no part numbers, vehicle makes or brand marks are readable on any mount.
No single item is singled out; it is not shown which mount or how many are being sold.

identity.kind: used car engine mount (engine seating), per piece
read_from: photo 0 shelf of rubber and steel engine mounts

claims.claim: For engine seating and engine mounting
claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows used engine and gearbox mounts.
Origin cannot be seen in a photo; no import papers or tags.
No close photo of any mount's rubber for cracks or separation; several mounts in photo 0 are heavily rusted.
An engine claim that cannot be checked on a loose mount from a photo.
Mileage of a removed mount cannot be shown; the heavy rust on several mounts in photo 0 suggests old, worn parts.
Reads as engine boilerplate; a mount is not opened, and nothing in photo 0 can show it.

risks.risk: Rubber cracked, perished or separated from the metal, so the mount does not hold the engine (hydraulic mounts may have leaked).
risks.proof: Close photos of the exact mount being sold, rubber side, from two angles, with a clip of it flexed by hand.
risks.if_unproven: as worn, near end of life

risks.risk: Mount may not fit the buyer's vehicle; no part number or make is readable.
risks.proof: Close photo of the part number stamped or moulded on the mount.
risks.if_unproven: as a generic used mount of unknown fitment

risks.risk: Heavy rust weakening the bracket or bolt threads.
risks.proof: Close photo of the bracket and studs of the mount being sold.

risks.risk: Quantity and which mounts are included are unknown.
risks.proof: Seller to state the vehicle, the number of pieces and photograph only those pieces.

proof_requests: Close photo of the exact mount for sale showing its part number.
Close photos of the rubber of that mount from both sides.
Seller to state the vehicle it fits and how many pieces are in the sale.
Photo of the bracket and studs showing rust and thread condition.
response.reason: Photo 0 plainly shows used car engine mounts, a plain part identified by type, so it is priced per piece at its worst case as a worn, rusted mount of unconfirmed fitment; the engine-style claims (no knock, low mileage, never opened) do not raise the price.
